newsitem.title: FRANCE: Russian-European group gets Globalstar launch deal.
newsitem.headline: Russian-European group gets Globalstar launch deal.

text.p: The Russian-European launch consortium Starsem said Thursday it had won a firm contract to launch 12 satellites for the Globalstar telecommunications satellite network being created by Loral Space & Communications Ltd.
Starsem said the contract, its first, was signed Dec. 3 but did not disclose the financial terms.

"The launches are scheduled for the end of 1998 aboard three SOYUZ-ICARE rockets from the Baikonour cosmodrome in Kazakhstan," the company said in a statement issued from its European headquarters near Paris.
Loral's Globalstar network eventually will include 56 satellites.
The Starsem consortium was created in August to enable European firms to enter the expanding market for the launch of satellites for mobile communications.

Russian shareholders own a 50 percent stake of the company, with shares equally divided between the Russian Space Agency and the Samara Space Centre. France's Aerospatiale owns 35 percent and the Arianespace satellite launch company 15 percent.
